Seen in the crowd at a football match at the Tooting and Mitcham ground was our old Club member, Alec Robertshaw, and we feel that any of our members, whether active or non-active, would be better occupied by an afternoon at Wimbledon, rather than by watching their local football team.

In 1929 Harry Hare, the first Belgrave President ever of the S.T.C.C.A., handed to his club mates the DEWAR Shield for winning the Championship (for the first time), and the six team winners medals to:- BILL MITCHELL (4), ARTHUR PENNY (7), ARTHUR ALLUM (12), BILL WEBB (16), PAUL KHLOPIN (23) and ALEC ROBERTSHAW (26).

Khlopin and A. Robertshaw, are deserving of the Club's congratulations and thanks for their efforts, as are also the remaining six members of the team who enabled the Club to become holders of the 'Colman' Cup in addition to the'Dewar' Shield - both for the first time.
The team was also placed in the National and South of Thames Senior and Junior races. BACK ROW (l.to r.):E.A.Duffett,R.Savage,A.T.Jordan,B.Lindsey,S.T.Ring,F.R.Webb,N.Dewberry, A.

Down at Wentworth, following the golf, who should TOM CARTER espy but ALEC ROBERTSHAW, a Belgravian from the "thirties". He now sports a goatee beard and is keeping very spritely, and passes on his best wishes to those who remember him.

The Belgravian Scribe was induced to write "The runners have lately been joined by W.G.Webb and A.Robertshaw and I suggest that the presence of these valuable men gives our team a new impetus of enthusiasm."

By Purley the black vest of Birchfield headed the procession and Alec Robertshaw, for Belgrave, had slipped to fifth – albeit a mere second behind the Army team Aldershot Command – but Belgrave’s own international Arthur Allum now took up the challenge.
